**The repo is already built for more than one app.** There's a single `APPS` list in `shared/apps.js` that the tile screen, the service worker and `github.js` all read. # Mine

Mine is a set of PWAs (Progressive Web Apps) to digitalize ones personal or professional life.
The key idea is to save everything in a repo as markdown files. This can be calendar entries,
diaries, markdowns extracted from voice recordings / pdfs / .. These .md files can easily be
ported to new apps without a vendor lock-in and are processed via an (AI) assistant to help you
plan your day, keep track of tasks, remind you of memories a.k.a. a second brain.

To keep complexity to a minimum each use-case lives in a separate folder. e.g. the calendar PWA
lives completely in a 'calendar' folder as does the zettelkasten and all the other apps. Each
folder contains a 'sample' folder with samples how the markdowns shall look, a REQUIREMENTS.md
describing how the PWA works and a TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md describing how it is built.

See [TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md](TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md) for how this is built, and
[TEST-REQUIREMENTS.md](TEST-REQUIREMENTS.md) for how it is checked.

## One app, one setup

Mine installs as **one** app on the phone, with one icon. The apps in the subfolders are pages
inside it, not separate installs.

This is what makes the central requirement work: **the GitHub repo and token are entered once,
in the main app, and every app in a subfolder uses them.** Verified on iPhone and Android.

## Main app

A tile per app: its `icon.svg` above its folder name.

Above the tiles, apps may contribute a summary. The calendar's shows today's entries and the
next one — which matters, because opening the app is the only reminder that works (see below).

## First run

1. Open the app URL and add it to the home screen (iOS: Share → Add to Home Screen;
   Android: menu → Install).
2. The setup screen asks for GitHub owner, data repo, branch, and a personal access token.
3. The app tests the connection and reports clearly if it fails.

Settings are stored on the device only. The token is never displayed again after entry, and the
app warns 14 days before it expires.

That's settled.

**Q4. What is the new app called, and does it replace the "zettelkasten" the docs talk about?** `REQUIREMENTS.md` and the README describe the planned apps as "calendar, zettelkasten, diary". The data-repo folder and the slug in `APPS` will be the app's name, so the name is the one decision every later step depends on.

**My recommendation: call it `notes`.** It gets a `notes/` folder in both repos and a tile labelled "notes". It *is* the zettelkasten, written the Keep way. In the docs I'd change "zettelkasten" to "notes" in the few places that list apps (`README.md:4`, `REQUIREMENTS.md:10`, `REQUIREMENTS.md:86`, the `shared/markdown.js:3` comment). "Diary" would stay in the vision text as a possible later app, so we don't rewrite your vision. The comments that use "diary" as an example of "some other app" (in `github.js` and `run.sh`) are fine as they are, so I'd leave them alone.

Is it `notes`, and is it the zettelkasten?

input.description: Read renderer checks in calendar suite

content.text:
I've checked the shared parts. The renderer (`shared/markdown.js`) and its `.md-*` styles in the base `style.css` are already shared, and the calendar imports the renderer from `shared/`. So a notes app can use it as it is, with no moving needed.

There is one real gap, and that's the next question.

**Q5. Should the renderer's checks move out of the calendar suite?** Everything that tests what the renderer does (headings, lists, checkboxes, bold, code, the `javascript:` link and `<script>` safety checks) lives in `test/check-calendar.mjs:2145-2185`. Those checks get there by typing a body into the calendar's entry popup and saving an entry. So the shared module that matters most for security is only tested by going through one app's UI. If the popup changes, those checks change with it. A second app would have no checks of its own on the renderer.

**My recommendation:** move the renderer checks into `test/check-mine.mjs`, the suite for the main app and shared code. There they'd call `render()` directly in the page on a fixed string, so no popup or saving is involved. The calendar suite keeps one check that an entry's body actually shows rendered.

The result is about the same number of lines, the checks are faster and less fragile, and they sit next to the code they cover. `TEST-REQUIREMENTS.md` gets the matching edit.

Move them?
yes, move the

content.text:
Done, that move is on the list.

**Q6. Should the main settings screen use the shared settings rows?** The Theme and Date format rows are built twice.
- `app.js:96-128` has its own `prefRow()` and a local `row()` helper, plus a `.prefrow` style in `home.css:55-58`.
- The calendar builds the same two rows with `row()` + `choose()` from `shared/ui.js`, styled as `.srow` in the base `style.css`.

The two versions already look slightly different, and a third app would copy one of them.

**My recommendation:** have the main screen use the shared `row()` and `choose()` and delete `prefRow()`, the local `row()` and the `.prefrow` styles. That's about 30 fewer lines, and the screen looks the same as every app's settings. `test/check-mine.mjs` changes its selectors from `.prefrow` to `.srow`.

I'd **not** add a shared `mineRows()` helper to save each app its two lines. Two `row(...)` calls per app is simpler than an abstraction.

Agree?
agreed

content.text:
One small bug I found along the way: `manifest.json` still uses `#faf7f2` for its background and theme colours. Since your last commit, `#faf7f2` is the *neutral* palette's background, not light's. I'll change it to `#EBE6D2` so it matches `index.html` and `--bg`. It's a one-line fix, so I'll just do it unless you object.

**Q7. What happens to the unbuilt "summary above the tiles" requirement?** `REQUIREMENTS.md:29` says apps may add a summary above the tiles, with the calendar showing today's entries and the next one. `REQUIREMENTS.md:162` relies on it: "The summary on the tile screen is the reminder". It was never built, and the README's Status section lists it as open.

This affects the refactor. If it stays, each app will eventually have to export something the tile screen can call, which is a cross-app contract. A notes app probably has nothing to put there.

**My recommendation: keep it as a requirement, but don't build or prepare for it in this cleanup.** No hooks, and no contract in `APPS`. Whoever builds it adds an optional `summary` to the calendar's `APPS` entry, and apps without one show nothing. That's a later, self-contained change. I'd only correct the README Status section so it reads accurately, since the main things in it are done.

The other option is to drop the requirement and rewrite line 162 so it says opening the app is the reminder.

Keep it as a future requirement, or drop it?
drop the summary above the tiles. I cannot recall this requirement and the calender app is currently fine and fulfills everything that I wanted.

Dropping it. While checking, I found a related doc error. `REQUIREMENTS.md:160-162` says alerts "fire while the app is open", but `calendar/REQUIREMENTS.md:722` says "Nothing fires while the app is closed. An alert is stored and exported, and that is all it is", and the code agrees: no alert ever fires. I'll rewrite the Reminders paragraph to match: alerts are stored and exported, nothing fires, and the summary sentence goes. The README Status section gets rewritten to "done" with no open items.

I'll also fix the line counts in the size table in `CLAUDE.md`, which have drifted. For example, `check-calendar.mjs` is now 2503 lines, not 2172.

That covers everything legacy I found. The rest of `shared/` is generic. `github.js`, `sync.js` and `search.js` already take the app as a parameter, and the docs record that the earlier calendar-specific bits were removed.

**Q8 (last). How should this be committed, and should it be pushed?**

**My recommendation:**
- **mine**: five small commits on `main`:
  1. delete spike
  2. remove Verify round-trip
  3. move the renderer checks
  4. shared settings rows on the main screen
  5. drop the summary and fix the docs (manifest colour, Reminders, README, CLAUDE.md)

  Each one passes `test/run.sh`, and I bump `VERSION` in `sw.js` because shell files change. **I don't push**, because a push deploys to Pages, so you'd push once you've had a look.
- **mine-data**: one commit through the GitHub API, *"Remove stale conflict files; plain README"*, pushed directly. It's dev data and has no other way to land.

result.output:
# Mine — technical requirements

How [REQUIREMENTS.md](REQUIREMENTS.md) is built. Everything here was verified against the live
API or on device on 2026-11-19; `spike/` re-runs the device checks and needs no token.

## Repos
**Load with `CORE_SCHEMA`, never js-yaml's default.** The default is YAML 1.1 and parses
`start: 2026-04-18` into a JS Date at UTC midnight — silently shifting every all-day entry by a
day east of UTC. `CORE_SCHEMA` keeps it a string and still handles bools, numbers, flow maps and
quoted scalars. This is the same off-by-one the bare-date format exists to prevent, arriving
through the parser instead.

## Platform findings

Verified in both installed home-screen apps (iPhone/Safari, Pixel/Chrome) on 2026-11-19.

| | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Storage shared across paths | **Yes.** A marker written by `/mine/spike/` was read back byte-identical by `/mine/spike/sub/`, both reporting `STANDALONE`. Cross-path module imports work too. |
| `{type:'module'}` service worker | Registers on Safari as well as Chrome. No classic fallback needed. |
| `storage.persisted()` | **Already granted**, no prompt, on both. An installed app is exempt from the ~7-day eviction that applies to uninstalled sites, so the token and mirror survive idle periods. |
| Quota | 35 GB (iPhone), 56 GB (Pixel), against a mirror measured in single-digit MB. |

Not tested, and no longer relevant: whether separately-installed PWAs get isolated storage. That
expectation is why the one-app topology was chosen.

Re-run `spike/` after a major iOS release — two of the four results above contradicted the
documented platform behaviour, and that is exactly the kind of thing that regresses silently.

- **the real device** — a system font scale, a notch, a software keyboard, Safari's and
  Chrome's own quirks. Serve the tree with `python3 -m http.server` and open it from the phone
  on the same network, or push and open the live URL.
- **installing to the home screen, the service worker and the update banner** — these need an
  installed app over HTTPS. `spike/` covers the platform questions and needs no token.
- **GitHub sync**: pulling, the one-commit drain, conflict files, an expiring token. Only a real
  token against the real data repo exercises those, and that is done by hand.

A change to any of those three is checked on a device before it ships, and
[TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md](TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md) records what was found and when.
